Beginner's guide · every screen explained

Your AI sales team for every exhibition

This manual shows you, step by step, how to set up and run the AI Sales Agent platform — the website chat, WhatsApp, company research, prospecting campaigns and reports. No technical knowledge is needed. Follow the sections in order the first time; after that, use the search box to jump to what you need.

AI talks to people The platform decides prices, limits and what is sent You approve and follow up

What this platform does

Think of it as four helpers that work for each exhibition — Build Asia, Health Asia, Pharma Asia and any you add later — every hour of the day.

Website chat assistant

Answers visitors on your exhibition website, shows the right stand prices, and passes serious enquiries to your sales team.

WhatsApp assistant

Thanks people who register for the show, answers their questions, and follows up with those interested in exhibiting.

Prospect finder

Finds companies on the web that could exhibit, researches each one, and writes a personal email for you to approve.

Reports

Shows where your business comes from — chat, WhatsApp or prospecting — and what happened with every person.

The one idea to remember

An AI is very good at conversation and not trustworthy with numbers or promises. So the work is split in two:

The AITalks and writesUnderstands questions, answers naturally, drafts messages and emails.
→
The platformDecides and checksPrices, the visitor's country, who may be contacted, limits, and what is actually sent.
→
YouApprove and follow upApprove content and emails, talk to serious buyers, record the outcome.
!
What the AI can never do

Invent a price, convert a currency, promise a discount, confirm a booking, guess an email address, or state something about your event that you have not approved. These limits are built into the software, so they hold even when the AI would like to be helpful.

Words used in this manual

An exhibition (also called an agent on some screens) is one show, with its own website, chat, WhatsApp number, email sender and settings. Everything you do on a screen applies to the exhibition chosen in the switcher at the top right. A lead is a person who left their details or needs a follow-up. A prospect is a company the platform found for you to approach.

A quick tour of the screen

Sign in at your platform address followed by /admin/ — for example https://salesagent.ecgateway.net/admin/. Use a modern browser; the screens also work on a phone.

The three parts of every screen

  1. The menu on the left — every screen, grouped by job. A small number next to an item means something is waiting for you.
  2. The exhibition switcher (top right) — choose which exhibition you are working on. Always check it before you change anything.
  3. The page itself — coloured bars at the top are messages: green means done, amber means "check this", red means something went wrong or needs you.

First-time set-up, step by step

Do this once for the platform, then once for each exhibition. Tick the boxes as you go — they are remembered on this computer.

A. Settings — the platform's keys

Open Set-up → Settings. Keys are like passwords for outside services; they are stored encrypted and never shown again after saving.

B. Agents and embed — one exhibition's settings

Open Set-up → Agents and embed and press Edit next to the exhibition (or New agent to add one). The page is made of cards; the links at the top jump to each one, and the Save agent bar stays at the bottom of the screen.

CardWhat to fill in
The exhibitionIts name, a short code, the website address, and every website address the chat may appear on (with and without www).
What this exhibition coversOne sector per line — tower cranes, building materials, HVAC. This decides who is asked about exhibiting. Without it, nobody is.
How the assistant talksIts personality, goals and selling style. Sensible wording is filled in for you; adjust it to your voice.
Website chatWhether the chat opens with four short questions (recommended: on).
Telling visitors it is AIThe line at the top of the chat, and your privacy notice address.
Where leads are sentEmail addresses for international and for local (Pakistan) enquiries, and your time zone.
Sales repsOne local and one international rep: name, designation, email, mobile, WhatsApp, WeChat. Visitors are given these when they need a person.
WhatsAppThe number, its own TextMeBot key, hours, daily limit, approval, and follow-ups. See section 8.
Prospect emailsThe sender name and address, the exhibition's own mail server, and the pace. See section 10.
AI and limitsWhich AI answers, a backup AI, a cheaper model for background work, and safety limits.

C. Content — what the assistant knows

  1. Load your documentsOpen Content → Conversation with AI, upload brochures, price lists and sponsorship charts. The AI reads them, asks you about anything that disagrees, and prepares everything for review.
  2. Check pricesOpen Stand pricing and Sponsorship. Every figure a visitor sees comes from here. International prices must be in USD.
  3. Add FAQs and knowledgeShort questions and answers go in FAQs; longer background (why exhibit, the audience, the conference) in Knowledge. Never put prices in either.
  4. ApproveOpen Day to day → Review queue. Nothing reaches a visitor until it is approved — by you, or by a colleague using a review link that needs no password.

D. Put the chat on your website

At the top of the exhibition's page under Agents and embed is the embed code — one line. Send it to whoever manages the website and ask them to paste it just before </body> on every page. The chat button appears straight away.

E. The scheduled tasks

Two jobs run by themselves on the server. Ask your hosting person to add them in cPanel → Cron Jobs (the exact lines are shown on the Settings page):

TaskHow oftenWhat it does
cron/whatsapp.phpEvery 5 minutesSends WhatsApp messages and follow-ups, answers messages the AI was too busy for, researches companies, runs prospecting and sends approved prospect emails.
cron/tasks.phpEvery hourHousekeeping, notification emails, collecting registrations, and a back-up run of everything above.

F. Test before anyone else does

!
After every update

When you upload a new version of the platform, open Set-up → Database upgrade. If it shows a number, press the button. It only adds what is missing and never deletes anything.

Your daily and weekly routine

Ten minutes each morning keeps everything moving. Numbers in the menu tell you where to look.

Every morning

Every week

The website chat

What a visitor experiences, and what the platform does behind the scenes.

When someone opens the chat

They are asked four short questions: first name, company, the country their company is based in, and whether they are interested in exhibiting or visiting. They can skip and just type.

  • Visiting — thanked by name, offered help, and at most one light suggestion: the conference, or exhibiting if their business fits the show.
  • Exhibiting — the assistant talks about exhibiting straight away, a lead is created, and their company is researched (section 9) so later answers are more personal.

Prices and countries

Prices depend on where the visitor's company is based. The platform decides the country in this order: what they say in the chat first, what they chose on the form second, other reliable information third, and their internet address only if nothing else is known and a price must be shown.

  • International companies see the USD prices you approved.
  • Pakistan companies — and anyone whose country is not known — never see international prices; they are passed to your local team.

When a person is needed

If a visitor asks for a person or a call, asks for a discount, complains, raises a contract, invoice, payment or refund, or the assistant cannot answer, it gives them your sales rep's full details — local or international to match them, both if their country is not known — and your team is emailed.

When the AI is busy

AI services are sometimes overloaded for a moment. The chat waits and tries again for up to about 25 seconds, showing "Still working on your answer…". If it is still busy, it tells the visitor their answer is on its way and tries again by itself. Nobody is sent to the contact form just because the AI is busy.

Knowledge, prices and approvals

If it is not in the knowledge base, the assistant does not know it — and says so rather than guessing.

FAQs

Direct questions with direct answers. When a visitor asks something close, your exact words are used.

Knowledge

Longer background: why exhibit, the audience, last year's show, the conference.

Stand pricing

Fixed packages or a rate per square metre, sizes in steps, tax shown on its own line. Every figure comes from here.

Sponsorship

Tiers, benefits and how many remain. Zero stops a tier being offered.

Conversation with AI — filling the knowledge from documents

  1. UploadAdd brochures, price lists and reports, and say what each one is.
  2. Answer its questionsWhere documents disagree or something is missing — a currency, a tax rate — it asks you instead of guessing. Your answer is kept as the reason.
  3. Review and addYou see exactly what a visitor would see, including price cards. Edit or leave out anything, then add it — as drafts or straight to the review queue.

Review queue

Everything new or edited waits here. Approve it yourself, or tick a batch and create a reviewer link for a colleague — no account needed, and it expires. Editing something already live sends the new version for review while the old one stays live.

Standard messages

Set-up → Standard messages holds the exact words used when the assistant cannot answer normally — the service is down, a price is not published, the AI is busy. Put them in your own voice; they are the messages that keep working when nothing else does.

Setting it up for an exhibition

  1. Connect the registrationsVisitors → Registrations: enter the registration database details (read-only access), press Test the connection, choose which of its events belong to this exhibition, then Start from now.
  2. Link the phone in TextMeBotLink the exhibition's WhatsApp number in TextMeBot and copy its API key. Every number has its own key.
  3. Fill in the WhatsApp cardAgents and embed → Edit → WhatsApp: the number, its key, Let me read each first message and follow-up before it goes (keep on at first), 10 minutes' wait, 20 a day, sending hours 10:00–20:00.
  4. Let replies come backPaste the webhook address from Settings into TextMeBot, so replies reach the platform.
  5. Switch it onTick Send WhatsApp messages for this exhibition and save. Test with your own phone first.

Everyday WhatsApp

  • Waiting for approval — read, change if you like, approve. The menu shows how many are waiting.
  • Replies are answered at once, day or night, and are never held or counted in the daily limit.
  • With a person — when someone asks for a person, complains, or raises money matters, the assistant steps aside, sends them your rep's details, and lists them here. Reply from this screen, then press Hand back to the assistant when done.
  • Stop — anyone who writes STOP (in English or Urdu) is never messaged again.

Follow-ups

When someone goes quiet, the assistant can follow up — only a likely exhibitor who never answered the first message (one gentle nudge), or someone who was talking about exhibiting or sponsoring. Ordinary visitors are never chased. Set how many (none to three), how many days to wait, and the last day of the exhibition — nothing is followed up after it. The AI may decide a follow-up would not be welcome, and then sends nothing.

■
The emergency stop

On the WhatsApp screen, Stop all outgoing messages stops every automatic WhatsApp message and prospect email, for every exhibition, at once. Nothing waiting is lost. A red bar reminds everyone until you press Resume.

!
Start slowly

TextMeBot is an unofficial service. A new number that suddenly sends a lot can be blocked by WhatsApp. Keep approval on and 20 a day for the first two weeks, then raise the limit gradually.

Company research

Before the assistant pitches to a serious prospect, it looks the company up on the web and scores how well it fits the exhibition.

When it happens

  • Website chat — when someone chooses Exhibiting, or later shows real interest in exhibiting or sponsoring.
  • WhatsApp — only when the assistant sees an exhibitor and they have asked, in their own words, about a stand, a price or booking.
  • Prospecting — every company a campaign finds.
  • By hand — Company research → Research a company.

How the score is made (out of 100)

PartPointsLooks at
Product fit25Do they make what the exhibition covers?
International expansion20Exports, distributors, new markets
Trade-show habit20Do they exhibit at other shows?
Pakistan opportunity15Signs Pakistan matters to them
Company strength10Manufacturer, size, standing
Reachability10A contact found on their own pages

90 or more is strategic, 80 high, 70 qualified, 60 medium, below that low; a company that does not fit at all is rejected.

!
Facts, views and unknowns are kept apart

A fact is only kept if it was read on a page the research can point to. Anything the AI worked out is shown as its view and never stated to the company as fact. Email addresses, phone numbers and names are kept only if they appear, whole, on the pages found — nothing is guessed.

Cost: each company uses up to 4 Tavily searches by default. Research stops for the month at the limit you set under Settings (900 by default — inside Tavily's free 1,000).

Find companies that could exhibit, research them, and email them from the exhibition's own address — once you approve.

Before the first campaign: the exhibition's email sender

Agents and embed → Edit → Prospect emails. Every exhibition sends as itself — for example Build Asia Secretariat <info@buildasia.net> through Build Asia's own mail server, and Pharma Asia through its own.

  1. Find the mail server detailsIn the exhibition domain's cPanel: Email Accounts → the mailbox → Connect Devices. Note the Outgoing Server and port (587 or 465).
  2. Fill in the cardFrom name, From email, mail server, port, encryption (STARTTLS for 587, SSL for 465), user name (the full address) and password, and your postal address.
  3. Set the paceStart with 20 emails a day, 15 minutes apart, and 20 researches a day, 5 minutes apart.
  4. Save, then send a testUse Send a test email under the form, and check your inbox and spam folder.

Creating a campaign

Prospecting → Campaigns → New campaign. Give it a name and an objective; list countries and product categories with the most important first (both optional); choose whether only those countries count; how many companies to find; the dates; and A person approves every email (recommended). Save, then press Start.

Approving an email

The menu shows how many are waiting. Open one to see why the company fits, the facts seen on its pages (with links), where the email address was found, and the email itself. The footer the platform adds — your details, why they were contacted, and an unsubscribe link — is shown underneath.

ButtonWhat it does
Save and approveKeeps your changes and approves. If your edit adds a price or a figure nobody approved, it is saved but not approved, with the reason.
Approve as it isApproves the email unchanged.
Rewrite with the AIThrows the draft away and writes a new one. Always shown to you before it goes.
Reject for this campaignNothing is sent to this company from this campaign.
Do not contact, everBlocks the company for every campaign, now and in future.

After an email is sent

Replies go to the exhibition's mailbox, not the platform. When someone replies, open their company and record what happened: replied, interested, follow-up required, not interested or booked. This keeps your reports true. If they ask not to be contacted, press Do not contact, ever.

!
Built-in protections

One first email per company per exhibition, whichever campaign found it; an address is never written to twice; unsubscribes, the do-not-contact list and the emergency stop are checked at the moment of sending; an email the mail server may have received is never sent again; and Pause or Finish stops a campaign's emails at once.

Analytics and the activity log

Where your business comes from, and a record of every action.

  • Choose the period — last 7, 30 or 90 days, this month, 12 months, or any two dates.
  • Opportunities by source — website chat, WhatsApp and prospecting, with interested and booked.
  • The chart — new opportunities per day; point at it for exact numbers, or open Show as a table.
  • Prospecting — narrow to a campaign, country or category; compare them with reply rates; Download as a spreadsheet.
  • Every exhibition side by side.
i
Reading the numbers honestly

"Interested" and "qualified" are the AI's reading or your team's record. Only booked means a booking — and prospect replies count only once someone records them.

Activity log

Set-up → Activity log lists everything recorded, newest first, each line marked AI Platform or the name of the person on your team. Filter by who or by area, or search for a company, email or event. Nothing in it can be changed or deleted.

Safety, privacy and control

The platform is designed so that a mistake by the AI cannot become a mistake with a customer.

Prices only from you

Every figure is looked up and calculated by the platform. A reply containing an unapproved number is thrown away and replaced.

Consent first

WhatsApp only to people who ticked the box when registering; never to people registered at the venue or on the do-not-contact list.

Never guessed contacts

No email address, phone number or name is used unless it was seen on the company's own pages or typed by your team.

Everyone can say stop

STOP on WhatsApp, the unsubscribe link or a mail program's button in email — honoured at once, for good.

You stay in charge

Approval before first messages and emails, the emergency stop, and a full activity log.

Keys stay secret

API keys and mail passwords are encrypted and never shown again. Changing a mail server removes its saved password.

Do not contact

Set-up → Do not contact blocks an email address, a whole company domain, or a phone number, for this exhibition. It is checked at the moment anything is sent, so adding someone stops a message that was already approved. Entries arrive by opt-out, bounce, blocking a company, or by hand.

Problems and answers

The most common questions, in plain words.

The chat button does not appear on our website

Check the embed line is on the page, just before </body>, and that the exhibition's Websites allowed to show the chat lists the address — both www. and without. Check the exhibition's status is Active.

The chat says the assistant is offline

Open the Dashboard: the assistant status says why. Usually the AI key is wrong or the account is out of credit — check it under Settings and press Test. Being busy never switches it off; the chat simply waits.

A visitor asked for a price and got none

Either their country is not known (they are passed to your local team, by design), or no approved package matches what they asked. Check Stand pricing, and that it has been approved in the Review queue.

WhatsApp messages are not going out

Check, in order: the WhatsApp screen for messages waiting for your approval; that it is inside the sending hours; the daily limit; the red emergency-stop bar; that Send WhatsApp messages for this exhibition is ticked with the number's own key; and that the five-minute scheduled task is running.

Someone replied on WhatsApp but got no answer

Look at Replies received on the WhatsApp screen — each has a note. They may be with a person, on the do-not-contact list, or waiting because the AI was busy (answered within a few minutes). If nothing arrived at all, check the webhook address in TextMeBot matches the one on Settings.

A campaign finds no companies

Check the research service is set up (Settings → Company research, press Test), the campaign is Running, and this month's research limit is not reached. Broad categories in plain words work best — tower cranes rather than a product code.

A company says "qualified — no email found"

Research found no address on the company's own pages, and the platform never guesses one. If you know a correct address, add it on the company's page; an email is then written for you to approve.

A prospect email says "not known whether it arrived"

The mail server stopped answering after taking the email. It may well have been delivered, so it is never sent again. Check with the company another way if it matters.

Prospect emails land in spam

Send through the exhibition's own mail server (not a free email service), keep the daily number low at first, and ask your hosting provider to confirm the domain's SPF and DKIM records are set. Personal, relevant emails at a slow pace are the best protection.

How do I add a new exhibition, such as Pharma Asia?

Agents and embed → New agent. Fill in each card, add its content and prices, approve them, put its embed code on its website, and set its own WhatsApp number and email sender. Everything is kept separate from the other exhibitions.

Something looks wrong — how do I stop everything quickly?

Open WhatsApp and press Stop all outgoing messages. Every automatic WhatsApp message and prospect email stops for every exhibition. The website chat keeps answering. Press Resume when it is sorted.

Glossary

Terms you will see on the screens.

TermMeaning
Agent / exhibitionOne show with its own chat, WhatsApp number, email sender, content and settings.
API keyA password that lets the platform use an outside service (the AI, Tavily, TextMeBot). Stored encrypted.
Embed codeThe one line that puts the chat on a website.
LeadA person who left their details or needs a follow-up.
ProspectA company a campaign found, to approach by email.
CampaignA search for prospects: which countries, which products, how many.
Research scoreHow well a company fits the exhibition, out of 100, with the reason for each part.
Handover / with a personThe assistant steps aside and your team replies.
Follow-upA polite second message to someone who went quiet.
Background modelA cheaper AI used for work nobody is waiting for.
WebhookThe address TextMeBot uses to pass WhatsApp replies to the platform.
Scheduled task (cron)A job the server runs by itself every few minutes or every hour.
Emergency stopOne button that stops every automatic outgoing message.
Do not contactThe list of people and companies never to be contacted.
